Hi Laura,

We're seeing a pronounced tail-latency and increased 5xx rate across our checkout traffic during the 22:00–23:40 UTC window on 2028-03-10. Our engineers collected traces and a telemetry snapshot (attached). The visible customer impact: increased checkout failures (payment declines that subsequently succeeded on retry) and average request p95 moving from ~180ms to ~2.4s. We estimate ~1.8% of requests experienced user-visible degradation during the window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood saw an internal event in that time range (deploy, cache invalidation, autoscaler activity, or routing fallback) and whether this meets the conditions for an availability/latency credit under our SLO? We need:
- a confirmed incident window you consider service-impacting
- the root cause hypothesis or an initial impact summary
- what evidence (logs/traces) you'll share for our audit
- an estimated timeline for a formal postmortem and proposed compensation (if applicable)

We're trying to reconcile billing for March and determine whether to file a formal claim. Please let me know the best time for a 30-min call today or tomorrow to discuss.

Thanks — Alejandro
Alejandro Ramos, Head of Platform Ops

Subject: Re: Elevated tail latency and 5xx spike on 2028-03-10 — initial findings and proposed apportionment approach

Alejandro — quick technical note from the preliminary evidence pull.

Summary of initial findings (preliminary):
- Timeline: 2028-03-10 21:52:15 UTC — first uptick in P95 observed; 22:00:00–23:38:43 UTC shows sustained elevated tail latency and a cluster of 500/502 errors coincident with elevated request queuing on the serving tier.
- Trigger: we observed a small phased config rollout to the serving pool (cache eviction enabled on new agent) at 21:45 UTC. The new config caused synchronous KV-store prefetch to miss for warmed-up sessions and forced more requests into longer execution paths while the KV cache warmed.
- Amplifiers: autoscaler activity around 22:05–22:15 UTC increased scheduling churn; combined with larger-than-anticipated batch sizes for some model variants, this led to request tail amplification for high-concurrency checkouts.

What we pulled so far: sample traces (attached in your bundle), serving-agent deploy log, autoscaler event log, and preliminary timeline (attached: prelim-timeline-warmup-eviction.csv).

Proposed apportionment approach for credit eligibility:
1) Define the impact window conservatively: 2028-03-10T21:52:15Z — 2028-03-10T23:38:43Z.
2) Attribute the portion of user-visible failed/slow requests that map to the serving-tier latency amplification due to the cache warmup event.
3) Calculate entitlement using the SLO's per-minute availability delta (we'll compute minutes where p95 or error rate breached the contracted threshold) and prorate monthly invoice value for those minutes.

Prelim numbers (ballpark): if we attribute the whole window as service-impacting and compute prorated entitlement, the credit falls in the range of a 6–12% adjustment on the March compute invoice for the affected tenant traffic volume. This is a conservative first pass — we will refine after correlating your raw traffic volumes (token requests / successful checkouts) against our ingress logs.

Next steps:
- Alejandro, please confirm you agree to the proposed window and grant us permission to run the full correlation (we'll need an exported sample of the March 10 checkout request ids to match).
- We'll open OPS-4721 and attach the full evidence pack.

Link to Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4721

Diego Fernandez

Redwood Inference

Hi Alejandro — following Diego's analysis, we want to propose the following remedial package now so you can proceed with your billing reconciliation:

1) Credit: Redwood will offer a provisional credit equal to 8% of your March compute/serving charges tied to the impacted tenant traffic. This reflects the conservative midpoint of our initial apportionment and is conditional on completing the correlation pass (expected within 48 hours). If further correlation reduces the attributable minutes, the credit will be adjusted accordingly; if it increases, we'll reevaluate upward.

2) Postmortem: we will host a 60-minute postmortem with your engineering and our SRE + product ops teams on the week of Mar 19. Agenda: timeline, root cause detail, remediation actions (changes to warmup/eviction toggles, batching safeguards), and follow-up rollouts. Proposed slots: Tue 19 Mar 09:00 PT or Wed 20 Mar 11:00 PT — please confirm preferred slot.

3) Operational safeguards: 2 weeks of elevated monitoring for your tenant (daily digest + actionable alerting) and a 1:1 onboarding with Diego to review batch/buffer settings in your integration.

4) Evidence & docs: the full evidence packet will be attached to OPS-4721 (Drive link above) and we'll provide a compact CSV that maps our ingress request IDs to your exported request ids to support audit.

If that package sounds acceptable, please reply with "ACK" and we will begin the correlation and formal paperwork for the credit. If you'd like a different credit structure (flat invoice dollar amount instead of percentage), we can discuss on the call.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
